title: NF1 vs NF2: The Ophthalmic Deep Dive
summary: A comprehensive comparison of Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (von Recklinghausen) and Type 2 (MISME Syndrome), focusing on genetic foundations, clinical diagnostic criteria, and pathognomonic ocular findings for the ophthalmic specialist.

rows: MISME Syndrome (Multiple Inherited Schwannomas, Meningiomas, and Ependymomas)
Neuroectodermal hamartomas affecting skin, nervous system, and skeleton.
Tumor suppressor syndrome characterized by bilateral vestibular schwannomas.
Lisch Nodules, Optic Nerve Glioma, Plexiform Neurofibromas.
PSC Cataracts, Combined Hamartoma of Retina and RPE (CHRRPE).

branches: NF1: Negative regulator of RAS/MAPK pathway
NF2: Linker between cytoskeleton and membrane proteins
Inheritance: Both Autosomal Dominant (50% de novo)

sections.title: Revised NIH Diagnostic Criteria for NF1
content: 6 or more Café-au-lait macules (>5mm prepubertal, >15mm postpubertal)
2 or more neurofibromas of any type OR 1 plexiform neurofibroma
Freckling in the axillary or inguinal regions (Crowe sign)
Optic pathway glioma (OPG)
2 or more Lisch nodules (examined by slit lamp) OR 2 or more choroidal abnormalities
A distinctive osseous lesion (sphenoid dysplasia, anterolateral bowing of tibia)
A heterozygous pathogenic NF1 variant with a variant allele fraction of 50%
A first-degree relative (parent, sibling, or offspring) who meets the above criteria

sections.title: Diagnostic Criteria for NF2 (Manchester Criteria)
content: Bilateral vestibular schwannomas (VS) <70 years
Unilateral VS AND 1st degree relative with NF2
Any 2 of: Meningioma, Schwannoma, Glioma, Neurofibroma, Posterior subcapsular opacities
Multiple meningiomas AND (Unilateral VS OR any 2 of: Schwannoma, Glioma, Neurofibroma, Cataract)
Pathogenic NF2 variant in blood or tumor

branches: Plexiform Neurofibroma (S-shaped lid deformity, 'bag of worms')
Optic Pathway Gliomas (15-25% of patients, usually low-grade pilocytic astrocytoma)
Pulsating Proptosis (Secondary to sphenoid wing dysplasia)
PSC Cataracts (60-80% of patients, often early onset)
Combined Hamartoma of Retina and RPE (CHRRPE)

sections.title: Optic Pathway Gliomas (OPG) in NF1
sections.content: OPGs are the most common CNS tumor in NF1, typically appearing before age 6. They are usually pilocytic astrocytomas (WHO Grade I). Unlike sporadic gliomas, NF1-associated gliomas often have a more indolent course but can cause profound vision loss, precocious puberty (if chiasmal), and proptosis. Screening via annual eye exams is mandatory until age 10. Treatment with chemotherapy (Vincristine/Carboplatin) is reserved for progressive vision loss or significant neuroradiological growth; radiotherapy is strictly avoided due to the risk of secondary malignancies and Moyamoya syndrome.

rows: CALS and freckling present, but NO Lisch nodules or neurofibromas.
Large 'Coast of Maine' CALS, polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, precocious puberty.
Multiple schwannomas without vestibular involvement or NF2 criteria.
Webbed neck, pulmonary stenosis, similar facial features to NF1.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Imaging
content: Step 1: Complete Ophthalmic Exam (Visual acuity, color vision, Slit-lamp for Lisch nodules, Dilated Fundus Exam).
Step 2: Imaging - MRI of Brain and Orbits with Contrast (Identify OPG, sphenoid dysplasia, or Vestibular Schwannomas).
Step 3: Near-Infrared Reflectance (NIR) or EDI-OCT to detect Choroidal Nodules (High sensitivity for NF1).
Step 4: Formal Audiometry and ABR (Auditory Brainstem Response) for NF2 screening.
Step 5: Genetic Testing for NF1/NF2 variants (Multigene panels).

rows: Surgical debulking for visual axis clearance

sections.title: RED FLAGS: Urgent Referral Needed
content: Rapidly progressive proptosis or vision loss (Optic Glioma growth)
New onset seizures or focal neurological deficits
Rapid growth or pain in a pre-existing neurofibroma (Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor - MPNST)
Bilateral hearing loss or balance issues in a young patient (NF2 Vestibular Schwannomas)
Severe hypertension in NF1 (Possible Pheochromocytoma or Renal Artery Stenosis)

content.explanation: NF1 is on Chromosome 17 (17 letters in 'Neurofibromatosis'). NF2 is on Chromosome 22 (2 acoustic neuromas, 2 eyes with cataracts, 2 ears affected).

sections.title: Clinical Pearls & Recent Advances
content: Choroidal hamartomas are now a recognized diagnostic criterion for NF1.
Selumetinib is the first FDA-approved systemic therapy for symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas.
Lisch nodules do not affect vision but are diagnostic gold; they are absent in NF2.
Always check for a 'Sentinel' CHRRPE in children; it may be the presenting sign of NF2.

sections.title: Landmark Studies: SPRINT Trial
sections.content: The SPRINT Phase 2 Trial (NEJM 2020) demonstrated that the MEK 1/2 inhibitor Selumetinib induced partial responses in 70% of children with inoperable plexiform neurofibromas, leading to significant improvements in pain and physical function. This shifted the paradigm from purely surgical 'watch and wait' to medical intervention in NF1.
